briefing.opening: Good day. We begin the Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Crisis in Multilateral Climate Diplomacy: COP31 Collapses Without Final Agreement
sections.content: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), held in Antalya, Türkiye, has collapsed without reaching a comprehensive final agreement following intense standoffs among parties over fossil fuel phase-down commitments [97, 109, 117]. Despite a year marked by deadly floods and wildfires across the globe, participating nations failed to produce a core agreement for the first time in 17 years, leading many to assess this summit as the darkest moment in the history of climate diplomacy [86, 117, 118]. In the wake of the summit's collapse, demands for an overhaul of the UN climate summit process have erupted, with some within the scientific community even raising voices calling for a boycott of participation in climate COPs and the IPCC altogether [84, 101, 103, 104].

sections.title: ⚠️ Compounding Crises in Climate Health and AI Power Demand Amid Worsening Weather Extremes
sections.content: Both domestically and internationally, the intensity and frequency of torrential rainfall have significantly increased due to heightened atmospheric moisture and weather stagnation [1]. With heat-related deaths hitting record highs, growing calls demand that climate change be declared a global health emergency, while elevated mortality risks are reported to persist long after extreme disasters such as wildfires and cold snaps have ended [3, 6]. Meanwhile, in the industrial sector, surging emissions driven by the rapid expansion of emerging technologies have emerged as a new crisis factor, as exemplified by Meta's greenhouse gas emissions skyrocketing 12-fold in a single year from AI data center expansions, effectively forcing the company to abandon its 2030 carbon neutrality target [58].

sections.title: 🌱 Scientific Advances in Ecosystem Conservation and Adaptation
sections.content: To conserve the Korean fir on Mount Halla—a species facing decline due to climate change—a genomic map five times the size of the human genome has been completed for the first time in the world [2, 83]. In Jeju's Gotjawal, research infrastructure and a standardized observation network for monitoring climate-induced ecosystem changes have been established, and phenological data gathered over eight months by citizen science seasonal observation teams has been shared as official research material [12, 13, 15, 18]. Internationally, a new modeling tool was developed to project climate-driven reorganizations of marine ecosystems, and the Global Fund for Coral Reefs successfully mobilized over $30 million in funding to protect coral reefs across 22 countries [90, 106].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Industry and Municipalities Expand Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Infrastructure
sections.content: In the domestic energy sector, Korea Western Power is actively advancing the development of the 504 MW Taean Offshore Wind Farm by repurposing existing coal power infrastructure, while SK Innovation has developed a key catalyst for e-SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) to help address renewable energy intermittency [68, 82]. At the municipal level, Chungcheongnam-do officially launched its Carbon Neutrality Support Center to manage emissions reduction performance, and Gangneung City is developing multi-leader smart orchards for highland apples in response to climate change [16, 41]. In addition, tangible energy transition measures are progressing across regions and industries, including the Seongnam City Council's passage of an ordinance supporting renewable energy streetlights and a private industry coalition's joint initiative to develop 1 GW of rooftop solar power [54, 73].

briefing.closing: Even amid gridlock on the international diplomatic stage and intensifying extreme weather events, scientific and technological adaptation research and field-oriented renewable energy infrastructure deployment continue unabated. This concludes today's climate briefing.
